page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture using AWS Neoverse-V2 Graviton processors. The configuration provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, using one thread per core to prevent hyperthreading contention. Cache capacity includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory is configured at 64.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps, features no discrete GPU hardware, and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence.

Benchmark testing demonstrates top-tier memory subsystem throughput alongside competitive multi-threaded computing capability. Large-block read memory bandwidth measures 390.52 GB/sec, while write operations reach 185.7 GB/sec, placing uncached memory throughput in the top ten percent of evaluated instances. The instance registers 21,777.0 in Geekbench multi-core testing and 47,220.04 in PassMark database operations, reflecting efficient parallel core scaling. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 365.93 GB/sec, static web serving throughput measures 74.43 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput attains 68.33 million operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including stress-ng single-core (1,706.99) and Geekbench single-core (1,893.0), perform within the median range.

The absence of local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators represents an operational tradeoff, requiring workloads to rely on remote storage over the 100 Gbps network interface and rendering the instance unsuitable for hardware-accelerated deep learning training. However, the dedicated core architecture and dense memory throughput offer predictable resource density without virtualization oversubscription penalties. The server is well aligned with multi-threaded code compilation, distributed in-memory caching nodes, high-traffic web servers, and parallel batch processing tasks.

The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz with 32 vCPUs, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-core allocation. Networking provides a high baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps, with zero local storage and no GPU accelerators. In performance testing, c8gn.8xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute and memory bandwidth, reaching 390.52 GB/sec in large-block read operations and a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,777.0.
